questions.question: _______ is a type of good for which demand increases as its price rises.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3 i.e __**Giffen Good**__

• These are **low income**, non-luxury products. its **demand increases** when its **price rises** because they are inferior goods with no close substitute available.
 
• Example of Giffen goods bread, rice, and wheat, etc.

 

**Capital Goods:**

 
• These are those goods** which are used to produce other goods and services.**
 
• They are also known as intermediate goods. Examples are machinery and equipment etc

 .

**Consumer goods:**

 
• These are those goods **which are used for consumption** and they are not used for the production of any new product
 
• Examples are food, clothing, etc.

questions.question: In Parliamentary proceedings, how many matters per day as per their priority in the ballot are allowed to be raised during 'Zero Hour'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1 i.e__** 20**__

**Zero Hour:**

 
• The time immediately following the Question Hour known as "Zero Hour".It is called zero-hour as it takes place at about 12 noon.
 
• .It was introduced in the Indian parliamentary affairs in 1962.
 
• this period, the members of the Parliament can raise important matters without giving prior notice.
 
• Members who wish to raise matters during the **Zero Hour** need to give notice to the speaker before the start of the daily session
 
• In Lok Sabha, **only 20** matters per day are allowed to be raised during the Zero Hour
 
• The speaker decides which subjects are to be discussed in the first phase and which subjects are to be discussed in the second phase.

**Mapping:** The transformation of data from main memory to cache memory is called mapping.

**Tagging: **is a term assigned to a piece of information. This kind of metadata allows the user to found the information again by browsing or searching.

**Swipping: **Replacing one segment of a program in memory (RAM) with another part of the program and restoring it to the original if required.

questions.question: With which of the following sports is the term 'twiddle' associated?
questions.solution:
Correct Answer is option 3 i.e __**Table Tennis**__

 
• Twiddle is associated with Table Tennis.
 
• Twiddling the racket means **rotating your racket** so that the backhand rubber becomes forehand and vice-versa.
 
• This is one of the most used techniques which is used by the players when they receive the serve from the opponent.
 
• This is one of the** best defensive techniques** used by the players nowadays.

questions.question: Flower colours of red, pink, blue and purple come mainly from pigments called _______
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2 i.e __**Anthocyanins**__

__**Anthocyanins: **__

 
• They are naturally occurring pigments belonging to the group of flavonoids.
 
• The red, pink, blue and purple colours of flowers come from this pigment.
 
• Plants that are rich in Anthocyanins are blueberry, cranberry, etc.

**Chlorophyll:** 

 
• They are green pigments found in the chloroplasts of algae and plants. 
 
• They absorb Blue and Red part of the electromagnetic spectrum so they are of green colour.

 

**Lycopene:** 

 
• It is also a natural pigment that gives the red colour to various fruits and vegetables.
 
• Plants and vegetables which are rich in Lycopene are tomatoes, watermelon, etc.

 

**Carotenoids:** 

 
• They give Yellow-orange and red pigments which are mainly produced by various plants and Algae.
 
• Plants and vegetables which are rich in carotenoids are carrots, corns, etc.
